# mhpfilter 1.0.0

## Changes visible to users

* Every function keeps its name, its arguments and its results, so existing scripts run unchanged; the results of
  every example of version 0.1.0 are reproduced to 1e-8. New arguments are appended with defaults that give the
  old behaviour (`log_scale = FALSE`, `criterion = "approximate"`, `fmhp = FALSE`), and the frequency `"monthly"`
  (lambda = 129600) is added to the comparisons.
* Every function that takes a series or a result is an S3 generic with a `.default` method. A `ts` keeps its time
  and frequency in the results.
* With `as_dt = FALSE` the filters return lists of class `c("mhp_<filter>", "mhp", "mhp_result", "list")` with
  `print()`, `summary()`, `plot()`, `ggplot2::autoplot()` and `as.data.table()` methods; the printed result ends
  with the sources of the method.
* No startup message.

## Speed

* Every filter is one pentadiagonal solve, O(T), instead of a dense one, O(T^3): `mhp_filter()` searches 100000
  values of lambda for 200 observations in 1.3 s (6.4 s for 0.1.0), and 3000 values for 500 observations 20 times
  faster than 0.1.0 (vignette "Validation and speed").

## Corrections

* `plot_batch()` passed `linewidth` twice (a warning) and ignored `highlight` in the faceted plot.
* The help page of `mhp_filter()` printed the factor of the criterion as `1 + 2/(T lambda)`; the code used, and still
  uses, `1 + 2T/lambda` (eq. 6 of Choudhary et al. 2014).
* `mhp_batch()` and `batch_compare()` accept series of different lengths (leading and trailing missing values).

## New

* `fmhp_filter()` and `fmhp_batch()`: the fully modified HP filter of Hanif, Iqbal and Choudhary (2017), with
  endogenous lambda and endogenous linear or quadratic end-point weights; it reproduces the published MATLAB code
  (`form = "rows"`, the default) and offers the penalised least-squares form (`form = "differences"`) and a fixed
  lambda (`lambda =`).
* `fmhp_compare()`: HP, modified HP and fully modified HP filters compared by the moments of the cycles and the
  end-point loss.
* `hp_loss()`, `hp_gain()`, `hp_weights()`, `hp_schedule()`: the end-point loss of Bloechl (2014), the gain
  functions, the filter weights and the end-point schedules of any HP-type filter. The end-point losses of the HP
  filter in Tables 3a and 3b of Hanif et al. (2017) are reproduced, and so are the annual losses of the paper's own
  scheme (quadratic weights, k = 20, alpha = 10) and the weights of its Figure 1a; the quarterly losses of its
  scheme are not, because the paper does not report the weights behind them.
* `mhp_filter(criterion = "exact")`: exact generalised cross-validation (eq. 5 of Choudhary et al. 2014) beside the
  published approximation; on the US series it is smallest at lambda = 1, which the help page explains.
* `mhp_designs()`, `mhp_simulate()`, `fmhp_simulation()`: the simulation designs of the 2014 and 2017 papers,
  simulated trend-plus-cycle series and the power comparison of the filters. The results of the comparison, for
  every design, are shipped and discussed in a vignette; they do not confirm that the fully modified filter wins
  in every replicate.
* `mhp_interpret()`, `mhp_cite()`, `mhp_app()`: a plain-language interpretation of every result, the references of
  every method and a built-in shiny application; `mhp_theme()`, `mhp_save()` (with WebP), `mhp_notation()`,
  `mhp_reference()`.
* Data `us_macro`: quarterly US real GDP, consumption and investment, 1959 to 2009.
* Quarto vignettes in HTML and PDF; complete help pages with the formulas; tests against both MATLAB codes of the
  authors and against the published values.

## Internal

* collapse is no longer imported; the help pages, README and NEWS are generated from roxygen and Quarto.

# mhpfilter 0.1.0

## Initial CRAN Release (2026-02-06)

This is the first official release of **mhpfilter** to CRAN.

### Overview

**mhpfilter** implements the Modified Hodrick-Prescott (HP) Filter for decomposing macroeconomic time series into trend and cyclical components. The package automatically selects the optimal smoothing parameter λ using generalized cross-validation (GCV), based on the methodology of Choudhary, Hanif & Iqbal (2014).

### Core Features

#### Filtering Functions
* `mhp_filter()` - Modified HP filter with automatic λ selection via GCV
* `hp_filter()` - Standard HP filter with fixed λ parameter
* `mhp_compare()` - Compare HP vs Modified HP for single series
* `mhp_batch()` - Batch processing for multiple time series
* `batch_compare()` - Batch comparison of HP vs Modified HP

#### Visualization Functions
* `autoplot.mhp()` - ggplot2-based visualization for mhp objects
* `plot_comparison()` - Visual comparison of HP vs Modified HP results
* `plot_batch()` - Visualization of batch processing results

#### Utility Functions
* `get_lambda()` - Extract optimal λ from results
* `get_gcv()` - Extract GCV value from results
* `print.mhp()` - Print method for mhp class objects

### Technical Implementation

#### High Performance
* Fast C++ implementation using RcppArmadillo for matrix operations
* Optimized grid search algorithm for λ selection
* Efficient memory management for large time series
* Linear scaling for batch processing of multiple series

#### Modern R Integration
* Full compatibility with `data.table` (≥ 1.14.0)
* Integration with `collapse` (≥ 2.0.0) for fast statistics
* Support for `kit` (≥ 0.0.11) utilities
* Works seamlessly with `tidyverse` (≥ 2.0.0) and `fastverse` (≥ 0.3.0)
* ggplot2-based professional visualizations

### Documentation

#### Comprehensive Vignettes
* **Introduction** - Quick start guide with practical examples
  - Basic usage and workflow
  - Comparison with standard HP filter
  - Real-world applications
  
* **Methodology** - Mathematical theory and derivations
  - Standard HP filter formulation
  - Generalized cross-validation criterion
  - Optimal λ selection procedure
  - Performance characteristics

#### Function Documentation
* Complete roxygen2 documentation for all functions
* Mathematical formulas properly rendered with LaTeX
* Extensive examples with commentary
* Author affiliations and ORCID identifiers

#### Package Website
* Professional pkgdown site with full documentation
* Download statistics and badges
* Interactive examples and tutorials
* API reference with search functionality

### Methodology Reference

This implementation is based on:

**Choudhary, M.A., Hanif, M.N., & Iqbal, J. (2014).** "On smoothing macroeconomic time series using the modified HP filter." *Applied Economics*, 46(19), 2205-2214. https://doi.org/10.1080/00036846.2014.896982

### Installation

```r
# From CRAN (recommended)
install.packages("mhpfilter")

# From GitHub (development version)
devtools::install_github("myaseen208/mhpfilter")
```

* R ≥ 4.0.0
* C++ compiler for building from source
* Operating systems: Windows, macOS, Linux
